corrections.original: Sutskever, Vinyals & Le scored 34.8 BLEU with one 4-layer, 384M-parameter LSTM
corrections.fix: 34.81 BLEU came from an ensemble of 5 reversed deep LSTMs (384M parameters each, beam 12); best single reversed LSTM 30.59, single forward 26.17; ~10 days training is per model.

corrections.original: AlphaGo Zero beat AlphaGo Lee 100-0 after 72 hours on a single machine with 4 TPUs
corrections.fix: The single 4-TPU machine was the hardware it PLAYED the evaluation match on; training ran on Google Cloud with 64 GPU workers and 19 CPU parameter servers (Methods). Do not say it trained on one machine.

corrections.original: Marcus had argued since 2012 that deep learning was only 'the beginning of the resurgence'
corrections.fix: Misreading: Marcus wrote deep learning 'may well be approaching a wall, much as I anticipated earlier, at beginning of the resurgence (Marcus, 2012)' - the phrase dates his warning, it is not his description of deep learning.

corrections.original: IBM and Microsoft subsequently announced improvements; Raji & Buolamwini 2019 measured them [KNOWLEDGE]
corrections.fix: Actionable Auditing (AIES, Jan 2019): all three targets (IBM, Microsoft, Face++) released new API versions within 7 months; darker-female error fell 17.7-30.4%; non-targets Amazon and Kairos at 31.37% and 22.50%.

corrections.original: Marcus-LeCun NYU debate, October 2017 [date not verified]
corrections.fix: 5 Oct 2017, NYU Center for Mind, Brain and Consciousness, 'Does Artificial Intelligence Need More Innate Machinery?'
Company 07386350 was incorporated 23 Sep 2010 under the name 'Friars 2022 Limited' and renamed DeepMind Technologies Limited on 15 Nov 2010.

corrections.original: Without the exclusion constraint the answer to man:king::woman:? is usually 'king' itself
corrections.fix: Nissim et al. report the aggregate drop (Google analogy 0.74 -> 0.21, 'in most cases' the second term returned) and use 'man is to king as woman is to king' as illustration; they do not report the specific king query. Say the method usually returns one of the input words.

corrections.original: Bahdanau et al.: each model trained for approximately 5 days
corrections.fix: Text says ~5 days but Table 2 lists RNNsearch-50* (the 28.45/36.15 model) at 252 hours (~10.5 days) on a Quadro K-6000.

corrections.original: 'Linear behavior in high-dimensional spaces is sufficient to cause adversarial examples' labelled a paraphrase
corrections.fix: It is verbatim from the abstract of Goodfellow, Shlens & Szegedy; relabelled.

corrections.original: GAN conceived at Les 3 Brasseurs and coded the same night 'by Goodfellow's own account'
corrections.fix: The story is MIT Technology Review's narration (Giles, 21 Feb 2018) with no direct quote from Goodfellow; attribute as 'as MIT Technology Review tells it'. Details (bar, sleeping girlfriend, worked first time) confirmed in that article.

corrections.original: Lee Sedol in 2019 credited his win to 'a bug'
corrections.fix: Yonhap paraphrase, not a direct quote: 'Lee attributed his win to a bug in the AlphaGo program.'

corrections.original: DQN reached at least 75% of a professional tester's score on 29 games
corrections.fix: Paper wording: 'more than 75% of the human score on more than half of the games (29 games)'.
Upgraded to VERIFIED-PRIMARY: Fig. 3(a) of Bahdanau et al. aligns [European Economic Area] with [zone economique europeen].

corrections.original: Hassabis: 'Solve intelligence, and then use that to solve everything else' [UNVERIFIED]
corrections.fix: Exact wording still untraced; verified alternative added: MIT TR (Simonite, 31 Mar 2016) - effort aimed at 'solving intelligence, and then using that to solve everything else' (quoted fragment in reporter's sentence).

corrections.original: Google acquired DeepMind for a reported GBP 400m (~$650m)
corrections.fix: Guardian text says '£400m ($650m)' but its own photo caption says 'around $400m'; reports range $400m-$650m (Wikipedia); never officially confirmed. Say 'a reported £400 million'.

corrections.original: Hinton (Axios, 15 Sep 2017): 'Science progresses one funeral at a time...' and 'throw it all away'
corrections.fix: Axios original unreachable (403); cite the epigraph only as quoted in Marcus 2018 (verified there); 'throw it all away' remains UNVERIFIED.
Guardian (27 Oct 2014) confirms quote and AeroAstro Centennial Symposium but gives no day; 24 Oct is unconfirmed in this pass.
